Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A strong thermal day with ample lift across most sites, but marked by a significant post-noon southwest flow increase that will challenge ridge soaring and create hazardous conditions at many launches. Thermal ceilings are high and lapse rates are sharp, demanding attention from pilots; the day transitions from gentle morning cycles to gusty, terrain-influenced winds by early afternoon.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — SE launch becomes cross/lee as SW flow ramps to 22–31 mph after noon; fly early. Best window 10am–11am with peak w* 403 fpm, ceiling 3466 ft AGL. Lapse rate 8.4 °C/km (sharp — advanced pilots only).
  • Hallelujah: Marginal — Wind direction favorable but speeds are strong; overdevelopment risk with 41% cloud OD and rain in the model. Best window 12pm–2pm with peak w* 524 fpm, ceiling 5505 ft AGL. Lapse rate 10.1 °C/km (sharp — advanced pilots only).
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — Low thermal ceiling (2438 ft AGL) and strong post-11am winds 25–28 mph create excessive shear (30 mph bulk shear) and limit soaring potential. Lapse rate is stable at 5.3 °C/km.
  • McClellan: Favorable — Strong thermals develop by late morning with manageable winds early. Best window 11am–1pm with peak w* 601 fpm, ceiling 6070 ft AGL; winds build after 2pm. Lapse rate 9.9 °C/km (sharp — advanced pilots only).
  • West McClellan: Unfavorable — Wind speeds rapidly escalate to 34–36 mph by mid-afternoon, far exceeding preferred limits. Limited post-1pm flyability. Lapse rate 9.7 °C/km.
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable — Sustained winds already at 33 mph by 10am and continuing through evening with gusts to 34 mph. Strong cross-wind component for the preferred southerly launch direction. Lapse rate 7.8 °C/km.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal — High thermal ceiling and strong lift but 50% overdevelopment risk and winds shifting across the E/NE preferred direction by late morning. Best window 10am–1pm with peak w* 614 fpm, ceiling 7373 ft AGL. Lapse rate 10.3 °C/km (sharp — advanced pilots only).
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — Excellent thermal strength with a high ceiling and limited overdevelopment. Wind light and manageable all day, peaking at 18 mph. Window 11am–5pm with peak w* 554 fpm, ceiling 6326 ft AGL. Lapse rate 10.1 °C/km (sharp — advanced pilots only).
  • Daydreams: Marginal — High overdevelopment risk (95%), though thermals are sustained and moderate. Best window 12pm–5pm with peak w* 275 fpm, ceiling 4347 ft AGL; cloud base within the thermal zone almost all day.

Hazards

  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Strong SW afternoon flow will create rotor zones downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range ridgelines, impacting Slide Mountain, Kingsbury, and West McClellan.
  • Thermal overdevelopment: Rainbow Ridge (50%), Hallelujah (41%), and Daydreams (95%) face significant risk of cloud formation within the thermal zone, with Hallelujah also flagging rain.
  • Low-level wind shear: Peak layer speed shear at Slide Mountain (6 mph), Daydreams (6 mph), and Duck Hill (7 mph) exceeds the 5 mph/layer threshold, indicating rough and variable airflow in the lower profile.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
